blocks.title: Field Notes: A Dawn at the Salt Marsh
paras: **5:42 a.m.** The marsh is still **mist-wrapped**. A **marsh harrier** quarters the reeds, **banking** low; its **flight silhouette**, wings held in a shallow V, **gives it away** at once. From the hide I **log** two **godwits** probing the mud and a **reed warbler** whose song **carries** across the water.

**6:30.** A flock of **dunlin** **wheels** and settles. I **tally** forty, though the **count** is **rough**; they never stay still. A rare **vagrant** from Siberia is rumored, but **patience** is the only **field skill** that matters. By eight I have **ticked off** nine species and **learned nothing new**, which is exactly why I come.

items.q: The writer identifies the harrier by its silhouette.
The count of dunlin is exact.
The writer found a rare Siberian bird.

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Forty roughly They never stay still

body: **A little bird told me.** — Um passarinho me contou.
**Early bird.** — Madrugador.
**Bird’s-eye view.** — Visão panorâmica.
**Birds of a feather.** — Farinha do mesmo saco.
**Take wing.** — Alçar voo.
**Feather one’s nest.** — Fazer pé-de-meia.
**Kill two birds with one stone.** — Matar dois coelhos.
**Wild goose chase.** — Busca inútil.
**Spot on.** — Exatamente.
**Once in a blue moon.** — Raríssimas vezes.
**How many dunlin are there?** — Quantos pilritos há?
**Forty, roughly. They never stay still.** — Uns quarenta. Nunca ficam parados.
**What is that low flier over the reeds?** — Que ave baixa é essa sobre os caniços?

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence diary entry about observing nature or a place at a precise time, with at least one hedge.
blocks.model: 7:10 a.m. The lake is glass-still. A heron stands motionless at the edge, then strikes. I count perhaps a dozen ducks, though the count is rough. A kingfisher flashes past; I almost miss it. I came to see nothing in particular, which is why the morning feels full.
